findings.title: Use a dedicated developer workspace for the OAuth application
findings.detail: Linear recommends a separate workspace for managing the OAuth2 application because every admin user in that workspace gets access to it.

evidence.quote: > [!NOTE] > It is **highly recommended** you create a workspace for the purpose of managing the OAuth2 Application, as each admin user will have access.

findings.title: Request the read scope for issue-title reads
findings.detail: The read scope gives read access to the user's account and is documented as the default scope that is always present.

evidence.quote: * `read` - (Default) Read access for the user's account. This scope will always be present.

findings.title: Do not request write scopes for this read-only feature
findings.detail: Scopes such as write and issues:create grant creating or changing data. This feature should not request them.

evidence.quote: * `write` - Write access for the user's account. If your application only needs to create comments, use a more targeted scope
* `issues:create` - Allows creating and updating issues, and creating their attachments

findings.title: Authorization request uses response_type=code, client_id, redirect_uri, state and scope
findings.detail: The documented authorization request includes response_type=code, the client ID, the redirect URI, scope=read, and a state value, which is recommended to prevent CSRF.

evidence.quote: ### Example ```http GET https://linear.app/oauth/authorize?response_type=code&client_id=YOUR_CLIENT_ID&redirect_uri=YOUR_REDIRECT_URL&state=SECURE_RANDOM&scope=read HTTP/1.1
`state` | (optional, **recommended**) Prevents CSRF attacks and should always be supplied. Read more about it here.

steps.title: Read the first page of issue titles with the bearer token
steps.detail: Send the first GraphQL query for ten issue titles with pageInfo. Expected response: data.issues.nodes contains id and title values, and pageInfo contains hasNextPage and endCursor. Record endCursor for the continuation request. Boundary check: inspect the granted scope on the token and the outgoing request log, and confirm that only a query operation was sent and no mutation was sent.
steps.doneWhen: The first page returns issue titles with pageInfo, endCursor is recorded, and the request log shows no mutation.

evidence.quote: -H "Authorization: Bearer <ACCESS_TOKEN>" \
--data '{ "query": "{ issues { nodes { id title } } }" }' \
} ``` To query the next 10, simply pass the value of `pageInfo.endCursor` as `after` parameter for the next request. You can do this as long as `pageInfo.hasNextPage` return true

request.example: curl '-X' 'POST' '-H' 'Content-Type: application/json' '-H' 'Authorization: Bearer <ACCESS_TOKEN>' '--data' '{"query":"{ issues(first: 10) { nodes { id title } pageInfo { hasNextPage endCursor } } }"}' 'https://api.linear.app/graphql'

steps.title: Send the continuation request with the returned cursor until hasNextPage is false
steps.detail: Use the endCursor from the previous response as the after argument. Repeat this request, replacing END_CURSOR with the newest endCursor, while pageInfo.hasNextPage is true. Stop when hasNextPage is false. Expected response: data.issues.nodes contains the next ten issue titles, and pageInfo gives the next cursor. Boundary check: confirm the request log contains only query operations and no mutation.
steps.doneWhen: Each continuation response is collected until hasNextPage is false, and the request log shows only query operations.

evidence.quote: } ``` To query the next 10, simply pass the value of `pageInfo.endCursor` as `after` parameter for the next request. You can do this as long as `pageInfo.hasNextPage` return true
and you'll paginate through all the values in the collection.

request.example: curl '-X' 'POST' '-H' 'Content-Type: application/json' '-H' 'Authorization: Bearer <ACCESS_TOKEN>' '--data' '{"query":"{ issues(first: 10, after: \"<END_CURSOR>\") { nodes { id title } pageInfo { hasNextPage endCursor } } }"}' 'https://api.linear.app/graphql'
